title: sse-partial-json-delimiter-token-ordering-fix
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Fixes multiple SSE streaming framing bugs that could produce malformed partial JSON payloads and out-of-order token/event delivery in the OpenAI-compat streaming path. Motivation: customer and internal fuzz tests exposed cases where structured outputs (function/tool calls and partial JSON objects) were broken for some edge cases (combination of chunked token boundaries + delimiter injection). This caused downstream SDKs and proxies to fail to reassemble JSON objects, leading to duplicate events or parse errors. The change updates the SSE framing state machine, normalizes delimiter emission rules, and enforces token->event ordering guarantees.

What changed (high level):
- Introduced a deterministic framing state machine that tracks JSON object boundaries, partial-object buffers, and explicit delimiter tokens.
- Normalize delimiter ordering so that partial-json delimiter token ("__redwood_partial_json__") is always emitted before an event that completes the partial object; ensures consumers see delimiter then content.
- Ensure token events (raw token stream) are always flushed in-order relative to higher-level SSE events (delta vs final).
- Added a strict fallback that, on out-of-memory or interrupted streams, emits a safe end-marker event so clients can gracefully close parsers.
- OpenAI compatibility layer: adapted the framing behavior to preserve existing semantics expected by openai-compat consumers while fixing the delimiter ordering bug.
- Tests: unit tests for framing state machine, integration tests that validate end-to-end SSE->SDK parsing with partial JSON and function/tool-call payloads, and a new fuzz harness for streaming edge cases.

Checklist: 
- [x] Repro case added in tests/fuzz/streaming_fuzz_test.go
- [x] Unit tests for framing state machine
- [x] Integration test with python/ts SDKs for streaming partial JSON
- [x] Updated compatibility assertions for openai-compat layer
- [x] CI green and manual verification with sample app

Compatibility notes: This is not a breaking change for normal text-only streams. For consumers relying on the previous (non-deterministic) ordering, behavior is now deterministic and correct; SDKs that attempted to rely on the buggy ordering should update to tolerate correct ordering (we already updated redwood-sdk-python and redwood-sdk-typescript in companion PRs).

Implementation notes: The framing state machine lives in runtime/sse/framer.go. Key algorithm: we maintain three queues (tokenBuffer, eventQueue, delimiterQueue) but serialize them through a single ordered emitter to guarantee token->delimiter->event ordering invariants. To keep hot paths fast we avoid allocations by reusing buffers from a pool and only snapshot minimal state for streaming checkpoints. A short snippet (conceptual):

  // conceptual pseudo:
  state.appendToken(t)
  if t.closesPartialJson() {
    state.emitDelimiter(partialJsonId)
    state.flushEvent(forPartialJson)
  }

Testing/benchmarks: Added a micro-benchmark that compares throughput and p99 latency before and after the change. No measurable p99 regression in common cases; slight increase in allocation for extreme interleaving scenarios but acceptable for correctness.

Related: companion PRs in redwood-sdk-python (PR #214) and redwood-sdk-typescript (PR #332) update streaming parsers to rely on delimiter-first ordering. Linear: ENG-1245 (root cause & fix), ENG-1288 (compat adjustments).

b4d9c50 - openai-compat: preserve compat semantics while fixing ordering

review_comments: Ben Liu: Please add a unit test that reproduces the original failure mode seen in the fuzz harness.
Aisha Patel: Added test that reproduces failure and asserts delimiter ordering; pushed new commit b4d9c50.
Carlos Montoya: Can you clarify why we need an explicit delimiter token instead of relying on existing SSE event types? Concern: size of events and extra allocations.

Aisha Patel: The explicit token is a small marker (8 bytes) and is necessary to disambiguate boundary cases where a token contains a JSON fragment that looks like a closing brace. We memoized buffers to avoid allocations; numbers included in framer.go comments.
Samantha Green (approver): Verified integration test with python and ts SDKs; all good. Approving.
CI Bot: linux-unit-tests passed, gofmt OK, integration tests passed on GH runners.
release_notes: Fixes an SSE streaming bug that could produce malformed partial JSON or out-of-order token/event delivery. Improves streaming stability for structured outputs, function/tool calling, and OpenAI-compat streaming clients. Non-breaking for standard text streams.
notes: Deployed to staging and canary; monitor streaming parse errors metric (streaming.parse_errors) for next 48 hours. Escalation contact: @Aisha Patel. Companion SDK PRs must be merged prior to broad rollout.
manual_verification_steps:
1) Run streaming demo with a structured function call payload that produces partial JSON.
2) Verify SDKs receive delimiter event before completion event.
3) Confirm no parse errors in logs.
4) Run replay from fuzz input set and confirm no failures.
audit: Recorded reproduction in internal fuzz harness and attached logs to Linear ENG-1245. All changes reviewed by runtime and SDK teams.
regression_rationale: Bug introduced during previous optimization that tried to coalesce small frames for throughput; edge case ordering wasn't preserved. This revert + structured emitter preserves throughput while fixing ordering.
notes_short: SSE framing fixes for partial-json delimiter and token/event ordering; merged to main.
